summary: American fitness guru and publisher Bernarr Macfadden built a magazine empire on fasting, anti-doctor health advice and tabloid confessions, starved his family on his theories, let his infant son die untreated and courted Mussolini.

evidence.note: moves to New York at 25 to reach a national audience
1941: shareholders force him out of his company
dies in hospital after trying to fast away a urinary blockage
stage shows and first fitness periodical launched in England
UK speaking tour and perfect-woman contest that finds his third wife
denies his wife a doctor and painkillers after childbirth
puts his seizing infant son in scalding water instead of calling a doctor
New York Graphic and fake composite photos as a political vehicle
deal with Mussolini to train Italian naval cadets, praised as proof of fascism
Salazar hands him children for a colony in Portugal

notes: Transcript gives birth as August 6; standard sources say August 16, 1868. Death year garbled in transcript; 1955 from knowledge. Opening segment on modern influencers (Rogan, Oprah, Covid) is framing comparison, so reaches_present is false. No role fits fitness guru or magazine publisher exactly. Italy setting is thin: the cadets were trained in New York.
